isme-2026.title_en: Five Vehicle and Energy Research Teams Receive Best Paper Awards at ISME 2026
isme-2026.summary_en: NTNU’s vehicle and energy teams presented research on intelligent vehicles, integrated energy systems, and sustainable technologies at the 11th National Conference of the International Society of Mechatronic Engineering, Taiwan (ISME 2026). Five teams working on hydrogen-powered mobile electric vehicles, hybrid electric vessels, autonomous driving trajectories, refrigerated vehicles, and thermal management received Best Paper Awards. The full paper titles and author lists are provided below.

kyushu-dual-degree.source_title: NTNU Vehicle and Energy Engineering Program | 2025 News
kyushu-dual-degree.summary_en: Graduate students Chi-Chang Huang and Quan-You Shi of the Graduate Institute of Vehicle and Energy Engineering passed the review of Kyushu University’s Interdisciplinary Graduate School of Engineering Sciences. They will pursue a master’s dual-degree program in Japan during the second semester of academic year 114 and the first semester of academic year 115 (R.O.C. academic years, as stated in the announcement). This reflects GPTL’s continued commitment to research talent development and international academic exchange.

kyushu-exchange-2025.summary_en: Graduate students Chi-Wen Chuang, Zheng-Wei Fan, and Shih-Lun Chou, along with fellow students, visited Kyushu University in Japan for academic exchange.

vehicle-energy-institute-2025.title_en: Graduate Institute of Vehicle and Energy Engineering Inaugurated
vehicle-energy-institute-2025.summary_en: National Taiwan Normal University officially established its Graduate Institute of Vehicle and Energy Engineering, holding an inauguration ceremony at the College of Technology and Engineering. The institute strengthens research in intelligent vehicles, new energy, and interdisciplinary engineering while expanding connections with industry.

hung-dean-2025.title_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung Appointed Tenth Dean of the College of Technology and Engineering
hung-dean-2025.summary_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung became the tenth dean of NTNU’s College of Technology and Engineering on August 1, 2025. His research and teaching have long spanned vehicles, energy, control, and industrial applications, alongside continued efforts to advance interdisciplinary engineering research and talent development.

eco-vehicle-2025.source_title: NTNU Vehicle and Energy Engineering Program
eco-vehicle-2025.summary_en: Students jointly advised by Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung, Asst. Prof. Chun-Hsing Chang, and Adjunct Asst. Prof. Yu-Hsuan Lin competed in the 33rd National Collegiate Eco-Vehicle Competition at Changhua Coastal Industrial Park. In their first appearance, the team won first place in vehicle fabrication and fourth place in the dynamic competition.

purdue-exchange-2023.summary_en: Faculty and students from Purdue University’s College of Engineering visited NTNU’s College of Technology and Engineering. Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung and graduate students introduced vehicle and energy research facilities and the automotive workshop, promoting academic exchange between the two institutions.

kyushu-agreement-2023.title_en: NTNU and Kyushu University Sign a Master’s Dual-Degree Agreement
kyushu-agreement-2023.summary_en: NTNU’s College of Technology and Engineering and College of Science signed a master’s dual-degree agreement with Kyushu University’s Interdisciplinary Graduate School of Engineering Sciences, expanding research and student development cooperation. Following the signing, Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung guided the visiting faculty through the automotive and electric vehicle workshop and related research facilities.

research-promotion-award-2023.source_title: NTNU 2023 Industry–Academia Collaboration and Research Achievement Promotion Award Recipients

neopower-startup-2022.summary_en: NTNU’s Office of Research and Development highlighted university research commercialization. Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung shared the experience of NeoPower Technologies, which he co-founded, tracing the transition from vehicle energy-management research to products and business applications.

green-transport-lecture-2021.title_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung Shares Innovations in Energy-Efficient Vehicles and Green Transportation
green-transport-lecture-2021.summary_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung delivered an invited lecture on innovative inventions for energy-efficient vehicles and green transportation at the training camp for the 2021 Taiwan Energy and Clean Energy Technology Creative Practice Competition. The lecture focused on energy-efficient vehicles, green transportation, and practical innovation, reflecting GPTL’s long-standing research and educational interests.

vehicle-energy-investment-2019.title_en: Active Vehicle Energy Management Technology Attracts NT$10 Million Investment
vehicle-energy-investment-2019.summary_en: Active vehicle electrical energy management technology jointly developed by Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung and Associate Prof. Syuan-Yi Chen received board approval for an NT$10 million investment from a Taiwan-listed company. The technology also received support from the Ministry of Education’s university–industry innovation R&D program, supporting a specialized laboratory, a technical team, and subsequent startup development.

michigan-collaboration-2019.title_en: NTNU Vehicle and Energy Researchers Begin Collaboration with the University of Michigan
michigan-collaboration-2019.summary_en: Prof. Huei Peng of the University of Michigan visited NTNU to discuss international research collaboration with Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung and university representatives. Focusing on intelligent vehicles and control technology, the exchange marked an important starting point for further collaboration.

industry-collaboration-award-2019.source_title: NTNU 2019 Industry–Academia Collaboration and Research Achievement Promotion Award Recipients

moe-industry-research-2018.title_en: Intelligent Energy Management Project Selected for Ministry of Education Innovation R&D Program
moe-industry-research-2018.summary_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung’s project on optimal system design and intelligent energy management modules for electric vehicles and green-energy facilities was selected for the Ministry of Education’s university–industry innovation R&D program. The project integrates electric vehicles, green-energy facilities, and intelligent energy management, with commercialization and startup development as major goals.

multi-energy-award-2018.title_en: Multi-Source Energy Management System Receives Honorable Mention in Energy Technology Competition
multi-energy-award-2018.summary_en: Students advised by Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung and Prof. Syuan-Yi Chen entered an innovative wireless-transfer active multi-source energy management system in the 2018 Taiwan Energy and Clean Energy Technology Creative Practice Competition, receiving an honorable mention in the collegiate local-practice category. The project integrates renewable energy, grid power, storage, and active power control to demonstrate optimized multi-source energy management.

engineering-education-2017.title_en: From Vehicle Development to Engineering Education: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung on Hands-On Teaching
engineering-education-2017.summary_en: An interview by NTNU’s Center for Teaching and Learning Development documented how Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung brought experience in energy-efficient vehicle R&D at ITRI into engineering education. It also followed students from ideation and frame welding to body fabrication and vehicle competitions, reflecting GPTL’s emphasis on hands-on learning, innovation, and engineering validation.
engineering-education-2017.source_title: NTNU Center for Teaching and Learning Development

intelligent-vehicle-2017.source_title: National Taipei University of Technology | 2017 National Intelligent Vehicle Scenario Creativity Competition

teaching-award-2017.source_title: NTNU Center for Teaching and Learning Development
teaching-award-2017.summary_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung received NTNU’s 2017 Distinguished Teaching Award. NTNU highlighted his integration of industrial technologies, electric-vehicle equipment, hands-on competitions, and problem-based learning into engineering education. These practices underpin GPTL’s long-standing approach to talent development through “Learning through Building.”

startup-program-2016.title_en: NTNU Launches NTNU Master Start-Up with Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung’s Participation
startup-program-2016.summary_en: NTNU launched NTNU Master Start-Up, a program centered on interdisciplinary practice and entrepreneurial talent development. Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung, then Associate Vice President for Research and Development at National Taiwan Normal University, helped advance the program, continuing his efforts to connect technology development, industry, and education.

greentech-2016.summary_en: Students Hsueh-Chung Han, Kuo Cheng-Ju, and Wang Ming-Yu, advised by Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung, entered the 2016 GreenTech TECO Technology Creativity Competition with a spring-energy eco-vehicle and received an honorable mention. The project demonstrates GPTL’s hands-on approach to turning energy concepts into student-built engineering prototypes and competition entries.

yulon-nissan-2014.summary_en: NTNU Industrial Education students Po-Lin Shih, 陳彥霖, and 游明倫, advised by Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung, won the Gold Prize in the Yulon Nissan Innovation Award with a magnetic vehicle anti-collision, anti-theft, and rescue system. Following Air Leaf and Endurance Life, the team achieved a third consecutive Gold Prize.

air-leaf-2010.summary_en: Prof. Yi-Hsuan Hung led a student team including Yu-Hsuan Lin and Jian-Hao Chen to the Yulon Nissan Innovation Award with Air Leaf, winning the Gold Prize in the Innovative Technology category on their first attempt. The concept integrated pneumatic energy with electric mobility and became an early representative GPTL student project.
